Subject: Pilot support request: digitized archives + long-context embeddings

Hi Sergio,

I'm Elena Morales, Director of the Digital Humanities Lab at Cedar University. We're planning a pilot to convert and analyze a 120k-item local newspaper archive (1860s–1940s) and explore search-by-context and long-form summarization for humanities researchers. Our group is made up of 5 grad students and a postdoc; budget is extremely tight for the next academic year.

We've used commercial trials for small experiments but the archive size and need for longer context/embeddings means the trial limits are a blocker. Would Redwood consider providing a promotional credit or extended trial so we can validate the pipeline (OCR cleanup, chunked embeddings, and retrieval-augmented generation at 65k token windows)?

Goals:
- Run ingest + OCR normalizations for ~500k pages
- Evaluate retrieval/similarity on long documents (multi-page)
- Prototype a public research search interface (read-only)

We can share a brief SOW and metrics we'd track (query latency, relevance by human eval, cost per 1k tokens). Happy to do an academic pilot agreement or acknowledgment in any research output.

Thanks for considering — if helpful, I can jump on a 30m call next week.

Best,
Elena Morales
Director, Digital Humanities Lab

1) Estimate: ingest (one-time) ~200M tokens for OCR-cleaned text; evaluation and interactive queries ~2–4M tokens/month depending on usage.
2) Prototype will be public read-only hosted on our university subdomain; no PII in the collection. We are fine with US-based hosting.
3) Preferred length: 6 months to cover a semester and some QA. Go/no-go: 70% of sample queries rated relevant by 3 independent human annotators.

We have a small discretionary fund but not enough for the hosting costs at full list price. If Redwood could provide promotional credits and extend trial limits (or unlock a higher token cap for the pilot), we'd be able to proceed immediately. I've attached a very short SOW (one page) for reference in my next email.

Quick technical note from Solutions Eng:

- For OCR-cleaned multi-page articles, we recommend chunking to 12–16k token windows with overlap for retrieval; this keeps embeddings efficient while preserving context.
- For a 65k token window RAG prototype, use a hybrid approach: long-context generation on a smaller set of curated documents and retrieval over embeddings for broader search.
- We'll run a quick cost estimate: initial ingest cost (compute + tokenization) and monthly inference burn.

If we provision the $8k credit + 10M tokens/month cap as Marissa suggested, we can likely keep average monthly spend below $1.2k after optimization — that should be manageable for the lab.

Happy to join the kickoff call.
